candidates.function: Place one or two whole units of an owned food on the ground as a paired exposure trial, inspect their quantity and decay, end the observation or retrieve what remains.
Plant one owned root unit in a small soil plot as a persistent trial, inspect a plot by direct observation, or take back remaining planted material; resume or cancel unfinished pla

execution.progress: Planting is paid work whose exact job and escrow persist across interruption; resume pays only remaining work and cancellation/death settles once. Inspect and remove are atomic one-round actions.

details.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1); two work rounds at one energy each, at an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; supply inputStackId. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy, the baseline probe observation of a plot in reach (target). Remove: one round and 1 energy, planter only (target). Tend is unavailable and spends nothing. No tools or water are granted.
details.effects: Completed planting places the real root unit in the plot; it keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Plot state records stage, observation rounds, soil moisture and temperature/rain exposure. There is no propagation, growth, harvest or replenishment rule for roots, so a plot never produces food. Inspect records only visible state. Remove returns only the material that physically remains, never a replacement; the emptied plot remains. Cancel releases unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for planting, inspecting or removing; genuine observed changes use the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback only.
